answer: An AI-agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with slashable stake bonds: each identity locks capital, and voting weight comes from that deposit, not headcount. Splitting one budget into many fake agents adds no influence, while a detected clone forfeits its bond. The attacker pays the locked stake plus the slashed penalty, and every extra identity multiplies exposure. Like a glacier wearing down a nebula of throwaway accounts, staking makes mass registration costly; a shared atlas of linked bonds exposes duplicates, so the attack always costs more than it gains.
